To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

semihydrophoic trickle electrodes made from crushed graphite and carbon black and graphite felt pretreated by electrochemical oxidation can be used for the electrochemical reduction of oxygen to H2O2.

the oxygen reduction to peroxide in semihydrophilic trickle electrodes prepared from graphite and teflowized carbon black occurs at a potential markedly more positive than in conventional graphite trickle electrodes.
the peroxide yields are higher for electrodes made of teflonized than of untreated carbon black and for electrodes made of oxidized than of untreated graphite felt.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of semihydrophoic trickle electrodes and the electrochemical reduction of oxygen in them.
the preparation of trickle electrodes and the study of their properties.
the possibility of using trickle electrodes as anode in a two-chamber fuel cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the peroxide yields in trickle electrodes are higher than in conventional gas diffusion electrodes, and that they can be increased by the use of semihydrophobized carbon blacks and pretreated graphite felts.
the use of carbon black in trickle electrodes is very promising and that the use of graphite felt is also possible but requires further improvement.
in semihydro-phobic trickle electrodes the reduction of oxygen to peroxide proceeds with high efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
semihydrophoic trickle electrodes are suitable for the electrochemical production of hydrogen peroxide.
trickle electrodes prepared from teflonized graphite and graphite felt are promising for the reduction of oxygen to peroxide.
the electrochemical properties of semihydrophobized trickle electrodes can be considerably improved by addition of a suitable amount of teflonized graphite or carbon black.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of semihydrophobized trickle electrodes is a promising approach to the electrochemical generation of hydrogen peroxide.
the electrochemical activity of trickle electrodes can be increased significantly by using semihydrophobes in them and that the use of graphite felt is advantageous for the production of peroxide.
the peroxide current can be generated in a trickle electrode at a potential close to the reversible one.
